criteria.name: Tip-over and overheat safety
criteria.description: In a small apartment the heater sits close to a bed, a sofa or a desk, so we score the two shutoffs and how hot the outside gets, from independent tests first and the maker's page second. Tip-over and overheat shutoff, and reviewers found the outside cool to the touch = 10; both shutoffs, but the grille or front panel gets hot, or no reviewer reported its temperature = 7; both shutoffs, but in an independent test the tip-over switch took more than 30 seconds to cut the heat = 5; no tip-over shutoff = 2.

criteria.name: Noise
criteria.description: In a studio the heater runs in the room where you sleep and work. Loudest setting, measured by CNN Underscored where it tested the model: no fan = 10, 42 dB or less = 10, 43–46 = 8, 47–50 = 6, 51–55 = 4, louder = 2.

criteria.name: Floor footprint
criteria.description: Floor area of the unit (width × depth) from the maker's published dimensions. Up to 40 sq in = 10, up to 70 = 8, up to 100 = 6, up to 130 = 4, larger = 2. A heater that can be wall-mounted with an included bracket scores at least 6, because renters may not be allowed to drill.

criteria.name: Thermostat control
criteria.description: A thermostat that holds a set temperature avoids overheating a small room and wastes less power. Digital thermostat in 1°F steps = 10; digital thermostat in larger steps, or an automatic mode without a set temperature = 7; adjustable thermostat without a set temperature in degrees = 4; no thermostat = 2.
